transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-06-18
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 mins
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Jordan (Redwood Partner Eng), Arjun (SonicWave CTO), Sofia (Cloud Ops), Daniel (Solutions Arch), Lena (Procurement)

Summary: quick partner discovery to understand SonicWave's hybrid GPU onramp needs — mix of on-prem NVLink racks and cloud burst, procurement constraints, SOC2/compliance, pilot/benchmarking required. Action items and next steps captured.

Topics: architecture fit, routing/burst, NVLink support, on-prem private deployment, KMS/HSM, SSO/SAML, performance benchmarking, partner commercial model.

00:00 Maya: hey everyone thanks for taking the time, i'm Maya from Redwood inference AE, with me is Liam and Jordan, quick intro?
00:07 Arjun: hey, arjun mehta, CTO at SonicWave. we build realtime audio transcription + recommendation pipelines, heavy token loads during events.
00:15 Sofia: sofia here, run the cloud infra and ops.
00:18 Daniel: daniel, solutions arch, i'll own the pilot work.
00:22 Maya: perfect, overview goal for today is to see if there's a partner fit to run Redwood as an onramp for your models — mix of dedicated + private on prem. can you describe current infra and constraints?
00:35 Arjun: sure. we have 8x A100 80GB nodes in our colo with nvlink fabric, then burst to public cloud when needed. must keep PII audio on prem for EU customers.
00:48 Sofia: procurement is strict — SOC2 required, SSO enforcement via SAML, keys in our HSM, and explicit audit logs. also network egress restrictions to avoid sending raw audio offsite.
01:05 Liam: understood — two quick things: Redwood supports private deployments with customer-managed control plane and KMS/HSM integrations; NVLink and multi-GPU affinity are in our runtime roadmap but we need to confirm kernel parity for specific models. we'll flag that for the pilot.
01:22 Arjun: ok, when you say "private deployment" do you run any agent in our VPC or is it fully self-hosted?
01:28 Jordan: good q. we do a hybrid — control plane can be customer-managed in your VPC while the runtime can be packaged to run on your infra. for air-gapped or strict networks we ship an on-prem bundle. there's a small management agent that needs outbound to our control plane for telemetry, but we can do a fully air-gapped variant if needed — tradeoffs on observability.
01:48 Sofia: tradeoffs are important. we prefer minimal outbound. can you limit telemetry?
01:52 Liam: yes, telemetry can be disabled or whitelisted; logs can route to your SIEM and only aggregated metrics are shared if you choose.
02:01 Daniel: performance wise, how do you handle KV cache and batching for realtime low-latency workloads? our p99 must be < 120ms for short queries.
02:12 Liam: ok, so we have continuous batching with traffic shaping, and prefix KV caching. but with NVLink and multi-gpu there's nuance: for very low latency we recommend fewer GPUs per request and aggressive KV pinning to reduce cross-device comms. we can tune in the pilot. note, p99 numbers depend heavily on sequence length distribution.
02:33 Arjun: sequence distribution is bimodal — short realtime snippets ~100 tokens and long post-event transcripts ~30k tokens.
02:41 Maya: thats a classic mixed workload. for long transcripts caching + chunking and using offline embeddings for retrieval helps reduce cost. on the pricing side, do you have target unit economics?
02:53 Arjun: we'd like to keep per-token inference cost similar to our current on-prem baseline — can't double cost. Also latency SLO for real time can't degrade.
03:05 Jordan: this is where dedicated pools + quantization profiles help. we can recommend int8/4 profiles for non-critical long-form tasks and keep fp16 for realtime. we'll propose a config in the pilot.
03:20 Sofia: security Q — do you provide per-request encryption with our KMS? can we keep master keys in our HSM?
03:28 Liam: yes, we integrate with customer KMS and HSMs. keys never leave your domain. SSO via SAML + RBAC is supported. audit logs can be pushed to your S3 or SIEM.
03:39 Lena: procurement: what's typical pilot commercial? we need a simple PO path and price ballpark for a 4-week pilot with dedicated nodes and engineering support.
03:48 Maya: we usually do a month-long pilot with reserved capacity + engineering hours. i'll get Jordan to sketch partner commercial options — low-friction pilot credit or short-term reserved pricing. we'll send a partner sketch after this call.
03:58 Arjun: also curious about failover — if on-prem cluster overloaded, can traffic burst to cloud (redwood hosted)?
04:06 Jordan: yes, smart routing supports policy-based burst — route by latency, cost, or region. we can configure automatic fallback to a hosted model variant but we need agreement on data residency and encryption controls for those requests.
04:20 Arjun: ok good. competitor question: we looked at OtherProviderAI and CloudTitan — what makes Redwood different?
04:28 Maya: quick callout — our thesis is serving-first: transparent perf profiles, unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private, and optimization levers like kv caching and quantization. plus first-class evals so you can tie regressions to prompt sets.
04:40 Sofia: i heard you do per-token cost breakdowns in console — can we see that during pilot?
04:44 Liam: yes, token-level billing, tracing hooks per request and per-route dashboards. we can enable deep observability for the pilot.
04:52 Daniel: about NVLink — is there a preferred OS and kernel for best performance? we've seen kernel-level differences affect throughput.
05:00 Liam: we usually recommend recent RHEL or Ubuntu LTS kernels with NCCL patched for NVLink. we'll share a runbook with exact versions in the benchmark doc.
05:10 Arjun: perfect. any blockers on your side to run the pilot?
05:13 Maya: none immediate, we just need access details, and a small security questionnaire answered. jordan will lead the commercial sketch.
05:21 Daniel: i'll put together cluster access by friday and include test data sets, plus a list of representative prompt templates.
05:28 Lena: procurement timeline — if pilot shows results, we need legal + procurement approval in 6 weeks.
05:33 Maya: noted. we'll align pilot milestones to that timeline so you have materials for legal.
05:40 (brief crosstalk)
05:47 Maya: recap — send security deck + SOC2 by 6/20, benchmark runbook by 6/22, schedule pilot w/c 6/26, Jordan to send commercial sketch by 6/25. any other asks?
05:58 Arjun: no, that's all. thanks.
06:00 Meeting ends.
